section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section provides the header information for the maamar.
section.t: With the help of Heaven.
Shabbat Parshat Ki Tavo,
18 Elul 5727

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section questions why the verse says "Your people, Israel" as two separate entities, implying they are distinct concepts.
section.t: "Look down from Your holy dwelling, from the heavens, and bless Your people, Israel."
And the Rebbe, my father-in-law, the Rebbe, precisely analyzes in his maamar beginning with these words
[which he said on the first 18 Elul upon his arrival in the USA for the second time, with the intention of residing there,
and the determination of that 18 Elul was on Shabbat Parshat Ki Tavo,
as in this year]
the fact that it says "Your people, Israel,"
behold, the people of God
("Your people")
are Israel, and Israel are the people of God,
so why does it specify both?
This is also perplexing,
for from the fact that it says "Your people, Israel"
(and not "Your people Israel"),
it implies that "Your people" and "Israel"
(in this verse)
are two different matters.
And it needs to be understood
(as the Rebbe precisely analyzes in the maamar),
behold, the concept of Israel is above the concept of "Your people"
[and this is also understood from the fact that the name "people" indicates
(sometimes)
the opposite of praise,
and the name Israel is from the phrase "for you have striven with God and with men and have prevailed"],
yet here it places "Your people" before "Israel."

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the two terms imply two distinct blessings, and questions the difference between them and why the blessing for "Your people" precedes that for "Israel."
section.t: And it can be said,
that what is explained in the maamar,
that from the fact that it says "Your people, Israel" it implies they are two matters,
is based on what our Rabbis, of blessed memory, said
regarding the verse
"concerning Shaul and concerning Yonatan his son, and concerning the people of God and concerning the house of Israel,"
that the verse separates the matter.
And based on this, it can be added,
that from the superfluous "et" we learn not only that "Your people" and "Israel" are two matters,
but also that in "and bless Your people, Israel" there are two matters,
a blessing for "Your people" and a blessing for "Israel."
And it needs to be understood the difference between these two blessings,
and that the blessing for "Your people" precedes the blessing for "Israel."
